question: When does the joining within the supreme become a manifest stirring?
premises: One supreme aspect can give rise to bliss.
Its joining produces a clearly manifest stirring.
The second supreme aspect is not by itself sufficient for emanation.
inference: Manifest creative stirring arises when the bliss-producing aspect of the supreme enters into conjunction.
uncertainties: The sentence continues into the next verse, so the insufficiency is completed there.
plain_english: then, when it is joined, a clearly manifest stirring arises; yet even the second supreme aspect, by itself, is not sufficient for emanation.
